instruction: In the vaulted water-store across the street from the bath-house, entered by the stair: at the window in its south end, below the upper outlet, 2 cubits: [deposit].
context: Redacted site description: a Roman country town buried by a volcanic eruption and excavated in modern times. Street fountains were fed by lead pipes from masonry water towers; the town had several public baths, theatres, temples and many house cisterns.

position.relative_to: street corner (north-east corner of a city block)

features.notes: Vertical groove for the feed pipe on one side; a small open tank once on top; impressions of lead pipes and some pipes preserved in the lime crust.

position.relative_to: large theatre (open space between it, a colonnaded forum and a palaestra)

features.notes: Deep; square outside and round inside; thought to hold water for sprinkling the theatre audience.

position.relative_to: temple precinct near the theatres (room at the south-west corner of the colonnade)

features.notes: At the left near the entrance of an irregular room used for secret rites; a niche on its north side.

position.relative_to: public baths near the forum (inside, in the furnace room)

features.notes: Beyond the three cylindrical water tanks of the furnace room; fed partly by rain-water from the roof and partly by a feed pipe from the town system.

position.relative_to: public baths near the forum (across the street from them)

features.opening: two stairways and three windows; the window at the south end is reached from one stairway
features.dimensions: about 15 x 4 m; holds about 360 cubic metres when filled to the window sill
features.notes: Built partly below the level of the sidewalk and covered by a vault; rooms once stood on its flat roof. Two outlets; grooves for a bronze slide survive. Probably built in the early years of the Roman colony.

withheld_question: How high above the floor of the chosen water-store is its upper outlet?
withheld_options: at the top of the wall
